I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou, that is still the safest way for me to earn steadily because the land, water, machinery, and my own experience all fit that system. At the start of the growing season, my winter wheat is already in the field, so I will manage it carefully through spring with one more topdressing, a few irrigations if water allows, and disease and aphid control only when pressure is real. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize right away to catch heat and rainfall, use a hybrid seed for stable yield, put most fertilizer in at sowing plus one nitrogen chase later, and keep the field clean and well-timed rather than chasing very high input. I would rather choose a familiar, lower-risk plan than gamble on a cash crop I do not know as well.
